correctness.rationale: Inversion of F_a(y)=(1−e^(−e^y))^a gives Q_a(u)=log[−log(1−u^(1/a))]. Differentiating gives Q_a′(u)=h(u^(1/a))/[u(−log u)], h(z)=z(−log z)/[(1−z)(−log(1−z))]. Its logarithmic derivative has numerator 1−(1−z)/(−log z)−z/(−log(1−z))<0 for 0<z<1, by strict log x<x−1 twice. Thus Q_b′(u)<Q_a′(u) whenever 0<a<b, and integrating gives every strict quantile-span inequality. Quantile coupling with two independent uniforms yields almost-sure strict contraction of pairwise gaps; exponential/double-exponential tails ensure finite second moments, so variance strictly contracts. Independently checked analytic derivative and representative parameter-quantile pairs; not a universal numerical proof.
